intent: Who has to approve a turf lawn or putting green in St. Augustine Shores, in what order, and what do the community's own recorded documents already rule out?
distinctValue: The neighbouring pages stop at county code, condo documents and the two Florida statutes. This page names the body that actually reviews an exterior change here and the sequence it imposes, from the association's newest published ACC application (revised 3 December 2025): the St. Augustine Shores Service Corporation's Architectural Control Committee lists a landscape project as its own improvement type, wants a survey showing the size and location of the work plus plans or pictures, must receive any drawing or survey bound for the St. Johns County Building Department, meets on the second Monday at the Riverview Club with paperwork due by 3:00 PM on the first Monday, can withhold approval over the grading plan, and does not review plans for county compliance. It dates the manual: the association's own documents page still listed the January 2025 ACC Manual in February 2026, and its website now opens a residents' portal with no public documents, so the page sends the reader to the Shores office at 790 Christina Drive for the manual in force. It also carries the community's own recorded constraints that bear on a turf base and a golf-frontage green: the deed restrictions' bar on changes in elevation that interfere with drainage, the Unit 6 rear conservation and preservation easement in which no fill may be placed or removed, the five-foot cap on fences and on hedges and landscaping along the rear and side lines of golf course, lake front and Intracoastal lots with opaque slats expressly prohibited, the eight-Unit structure that decides which deed restrictions apply to a given address, and the verified absence of any mention of artificial turf in either the manual or the December 2025 application, which is why the page tells the reader to put the question to the committee in writing.

sources.label: St. Augustine Shores Service Corporation: Architectural Control Committee application, Rev. 12.3.25 (Internet Archive copy of staugshores.com, captured 17 March 2026)
supports: Header: "ARCHITECTURAL CONTROL COMMITTEE / 790 Christina Drive, St. Augustine, Florida 32086"; footer "Rev. 12.3.25".
"CHECK DESCRIPTION OF IMPROVEMENT" lists, among others, "Landscape Project", "Paver /Patio Project", "Fences/Walls" and "Other". No box names artificial turf or a putting green.
"I hereby agree to not begin any improvements or changes until the ACC (Architectural Control Committee) notifies me of their approval."

"I understand that plans and specifications submitted for review are not being reviewed for structural integrity; compliance with zoning and building ordinances or any other applicable statutes, ordinances or governmental rules or regulations, compliance with the requirements of any public utility, easement or other agreements, or preservation of any view."
"Applicants are responsible to sod swales abutting property and installing and/or repairing any portion of the sidewalk that is missing or damaged."
"This application is valid for thirty (30) days from date of approval."

Checklist: "Attach official property survey showing dimensions/location of proposed project on property" and "Attach pictures/plans of design, layout, elevation, finish, paint color- to show appearance of finished product/improvement"; "Landscape plans (for new homes)".
Requirement 1: "Meetings are held on the 2nd (second) Monday of each month at 6:00PM at Riverview Club. Homeowner or contractor should attend meeting. Any incomplete applications will be rejected."

Requirement 2: "All paperwork must be submitted by 3:00PM on the 1st (first) Monday of the month for review." (The 8 September 2025 revision said 5:00PM; this is the only text change between the two revisions.)
Requirement 5: "All drawings submitted to St. Johns County Building Dept., including surveys, must be submitted to the St. Augustine Shores Architectural Control Committee."
Requirement 6: "It is the property owner's responsibility to review the lot line setback requirements per the ACC Manual based upon the property's unit prior to installation."

Requirement 8: "The approval of said plans and specifications may be withheld, not only because of their non-compliance with any of the specific restrictions contained in this and other clauses hereof, but also by reason of reasonable dissatisfaction of the ACC or it's agent with the grading plan, location of the structure on the building site".
Verified absence: full-text search of the extracted application returns zero occurrences of "turf", "synthetic" or "artificial".

sources.label: St. Augustine Shores Service Corporation: Architectural Control Committee Manual, January 2025 (Internet Archive copy of staugshores.com, captured 4 May 2025; still the manual listed on the association's documents page in February 2026)
supports: Cover: "St. Augustine Shores Service Corporation / Architectural Control Committee Manual (ACC FINAL) / REVISED AS PER 2024 LEGISLATIVE CHANGES SIGNED BY GOVERNOR RON DESANTIS / January 2025".

Section 1A: "The St. Augustine Shores Service Corporation Board of Directors, hereinafter referred to as the BOD, on January 9, 2025, has approved this manual outlining the requirements, and guidelines contained herein as intended for the use of the property owners in the St. Augustine Shores Sub Division".
Section 4E: "All drawings submitted to St. Johns County Building Department, including surveys, must first be submitted to the St. Augustine Shores Architectural Control Committee."

Section 4A: "Homeowner or contractor should attend meeting. If there are any questions or issues and there is no one at the meeting representing the applicant, the application may be tabled until the next scheduled meeting."

Section 4B: "All paperwork must be submitted to the St. Augustine Shores office at least one week prior to the meeting for review. There is a charge for each application. The homeowner must sign the application."
Section 7B: "The ACC shall have thirty (30) days for review and approval or rejection of submitted drawings."

Section 3A: "No residences, lot or property, additions thereto, add-ons, accessories, pools, fences or any other such structures, shall be erected, placed, constructed, altered or maintained upon any portion of said lots, unless a complete set of plans and specifications together with a plot plan indicating the exact location on the building site, shall have been submitted to, and approved by the ACC in writing."

Section 3A: "The approval of said plans and specifications may be withheld, not only because of their noncompliance with any of the specific restrictions contained in this and other clauses hereof, but also by reason of the reasonable dissatisfaction of the ACC or its agent with the grading plan, location of the structure on the building site".

Section 13A(d): "Fences on golf course, lake front, or intra-costal lots shall be limited to a maximum height of five (5) feet, and shall not interfere with rear or side site line view. A chain link fence or other open fencing may be used on these properties, however, visual barriers, such as but not limited to, opaque slats within or attached to chain link fencing are expressly prohibited. Any solid or opaque fence or wall comprised of any other material shall be limited to a maximum height of five (5) feet. Hedges or other landscaping along the rear and/or side property lines along said lots shall also be limited to a maximum height of five (5) feet."

Section 6B: "Unit 6 There shall be a conservation and preservation easement along the rear property line of the following described lots for the purpose of protecting and preserving a natural stream bed which runs along the boundary of said lots. No construction or alteration including the placement or removal of all fill materials or the construction of any fence, wall, or similar obstruction shall be permitted within any portion of any lot lying within such easement."
Section 7I6: "All swales and lots (front, sides and rear) should be sodded. In-ground sprinkler systems are permitted on lots."

Section 7G1c: "All sodded (front, sides, rear and swales) and landscaped areas (showing type, quantity and location of landscaping) and location of trees sought to be removed should be on the drawing. Specimen trees should be kept if possible. Stones or bushes in lieu of sod are not desirable; however, appropriate landscaping will be considered."

Section 1C: "The ACC does not enforce County requirements, Southern Building Code requirements, or other regulatory agency requirements, but does advise the property owner when these permits are also required."
Section 5A gives a separate setback table for each of Units 1 through 8.

Verified absence: a full-text search of the extracted manual returns zero occurrences of "turf", "synthetic" or "artificial grass". The only occurrence of "artificial" is in the swimming-pool definition, "capable of containing an artificial body of water".

sources.label: Florida Legislature: 2026 Section 720.3045
supports: Independently retrieved the current official text on September 12. Its association restriction test covers visibility from the parcel frontage, adjacent parcels, adjacent common areas and a community golf course; it also retains the exception for prohibitions under general law or local ordinance. Fencing alone does not establish that the test is met.

reviewNotes: The association's own domains (staugshores.com, www.staugshores.com, staugshores.org, staugshores.net) now 301 to https://engage.goenumerate.com/s/StAugustineShores/ for every path. That resident portal publishes a contact page and pool and club pages to the public, but its Resources page lists only a payment link and its forms sit behind a login. No ACC manual, ACC application or deed restriction is publicly available from the association as of September 12, 2026.

The newest official copies found are Internet Archive captures of the old site: the Documents page of 15 February 2026, which still links the January 2025 ACC Manual and the ACC application Rev. 12.3.25, and the application itself, captured 17 March 2026. The archive's upload listing through the last site capture (17 May 2026) shows no later ACC manual. The page dates both documents and tells the reader to get the manual and form in force from the Shores office.

The December 2025 application's paperwork deadline (3:00PM on the first Monday, meetings on the second Monday) is consistent with the manual's one-week rule; the page uses the application's wording because it is the newer document. The application's 30-day validity after approval is a different period from the manual's 30-day review period, and the page cites only the review period.

The ACC manual and application are the association's own documents, not public ordinance. Both say the ACC does not review for county or other regulatory compliance, so nothing here displaces St. Johns County review or the two Florida statutes already cited on the page.

Neither the manual nor the application names artificial turf or putting greens; the application's closest category is "Landscape Project". The page therefore does not claim the ACC permits or forbids turf, does not say turf is filed as a landscape project, and tells the reader to put the question to the committee in writing.

The Unit 6 conservation and preservation easement applies to named lots in one block, recorded at Book 482/Page 201. The page refers to it as certain lots in Unit 6 rather than listing them, and tells the reader to check their own Unit's recorded restrictions.

Application fees, pool and club rates, and monthly assessments appear in these documents and are deliberately left off the page. Staff names on the contact page and in the notices are left off the page as well; only the office address is used.
The eight Unit deed restriction PDFs were not re-read in this pass: the Internet Archive returned no 2026 capture for six of them and truncated the other two.
unresolved: The ACC manual in force on September 12, 2026 could not be read: the association now keeps its documents behind a resident-portal login. The most recent public evidence (Documents page, 15 February 2026) shows the January 2025 manual and the December 2025 application as current then, and neither names artificial turf. Whether the committee has since revised either document, and how it treats a synthetic-turf lawn or putting green, can only be confirmed with the Shores office at 790 Christina Drive (904-797-6441).
Not established: whether any Unit's recorded deed restrictions name turf, or which Unit any particular address falls in.
